name: Pennsylvania

agency.name: Pennsylvania Department of Transportation, Driver and Vehicle Services

gaps: The trade-in deduction from the taxable price is applied as in Pennsylvania's sales tax law; the statute itself could not be opened during this reading (the legislature site refused the request).
Safety and emissions inspections are done by private stations whose prices PennDOT does not set; the inspection is listed without an amount.
On a used car, the Department of Revenue can assess tax on fair market value when the stated price is far below it; the engine taxes the price.
No legal maximum for the dealer documentation fee was found in the PennDOT and Revenue pages read; the calculator uses the figure you type.

summary.docFeeNote: No cap found in the official pages read for this release; type the dealer's fee.
summary.inspectionWhere: Yearly safety inspection for most passenger cars and light trucks statewide, plus an emissions inspection in the counties of the state's emissions program; stations set the price.

inspection.label: Yearly safety inspection (station price)
inspection.note: Valid one year; price set by the inspection station.

singular: Pennsylvania adds 2% to its 6% sales tax in Philadelphia and 1% in Allegheny County; everywhere else the rate on a car is 6% [rev-sut].
Registering a passenger car costs a flat $48 a year, and the fee includes the first standard plate [mv70s].
A Pennsylvania title costs $72, and recording a lien adds $36 per lien [mv70s].
Since 2025 electric cars pay a road user charge with registration: $250 for one year or $500 for two in 2026, and plug-in hybrids pay a quarter of it, $63 [ruc].
From January 1, 2027 the road user charge follows the consumer price index each year [ruc].
27 counties, Philadelphia and Allegheny among them, add a $5 yearly fee for local use collected by PennDOT with registration [local-fee].
If a used car's stated price is far below its fair market value, the Department of Revenue can bill the tax on the fair market value under its understated value program [rev-uv].
Most cars need a yearly safety inspection, with a sticker valid one year from the month of inspection [safety-faq].

mv70s.name: PennDOT Form MV-70S, Bureau of Motor Vehicles Schedule of Fees
mv70s.quote: *Passenger $48.00 $96.00 ... Certificate of Title $72.00 ... Recording a Lien ... $36.00 ... 1 Year Registration $250 $63

ruc.name: PennDOT, Road User Charge for Electric and Plug-In Hybrid Vehicles
ruc.quote: 2026 | One year: $250 Two year: $500 | One year: $63 Two year: $126 | Each Jan. 1 thereafter | Tied to consumer price index (CPI)

rev-sut.name: Pennsylvania Department of Revenue, Sales, Use and Hotel Occupancy Tax
rev-sut.quote: The Pennsylvania sales tax rate is 6 percent. By law, a 1 percent local tax is added to purchases made in Allegheny County, and 2 percent local tax is added to purchases made in Philadelphia.

rev-uv.name: Pennsylvania Department of Revenue, Motor Vehicle Understated Value Program
rev-uv.quote: additional sales tax may be due in cases where a vehicle’s purchase price is significantly lower than fair market value

local-fee.name: PennDOT Fact Sheet, Fee for Local Use, Participating Counties
local-fee.quote: a county may pass an ordinance to implement an annual fee of $5 for each vehicle registered to an address located in that county

safety-faq.name: PennDOT, Safety Inspection Program (For Consumers) FAQs
safety-faq.quote: Upon passing a safety inspection, most passenger cars and light trucks will receive an inspection sticker valid for one year from the month of inspection
